intro: Crispy battered chicken chunks tossed in a sticky-sweet sesame glaze, topped with toasted sesame seeds. An American-Chinese takeout staple.
Crispy battered chicken in a sweet-spicy glaze with dried chilies and scallions. Named after a 19th-century Hunan military leader, but invented in 1950s New York.

Six deep-fried chicken wings served with a side of spicy sauce. Crispy outside, juicy inside.

Bite-sized crispy fried chicken pieces seasoned with salt, pepper, and basil. A Taiwanese night market classic.
Bouncy fish balls simmered in a sweet-spicy Hong Kong-style curry sauce. A street-food classic.
Whole chicken poached in a master stock of soy sauce, sugar, ginger, and star anise until mahogany and silky. Cantonese siu mei classic.

Hong Kong-style curry beef stew with potato and carrot, ladled over steamed rice.

intro: Hong Kong-style beef brisket stew in a savory tomato broth, ladled over steamed rice.
Half duck with shatteringly crisp skin lacquered in maltose, served with steamed pancakes, scallion brushes, cucumber, and hoisin sauce. A Beijing imperial tradition since the Yuan dynasty.
Slow-braised beef brisket in a soy-ginger master stock with star anise, served sizzling in a claypot. A Nanyang (SE Asia) adaptation of a Henan classic.
Tender beef brisket and Chinese yam slow-braised in a savory master stock until silky. Warming and earthy.

pinyin: lao tang lu shui dou fu
intro: Soft tofu wedges braised in a soy-and-spice master stock until they soak up a deep mahogany color. Shaanxi-style snack.

pinyin: lao bei jing zha jiang mian
intro: Hand-pulled wheat noodles topped with fermented yellow soybean paste and ground pork, garnished with crisp cucumber, edamame, radish, and celery. A Beijing breakfast and lunch staple.
Wide hand-pulled Shaanxi noodles drenched in smoking-hot chili oil poured over scallions and garlic at the table. Loud sizzle, deep fragrance.
Thick, irregular hand-shaved noodles with chewy edges, served in a clear tomato-egg broth or a savory meat sauce. Shanxi province specialty.

pinyin: lan zhou niu rou la mian
intro: Lanzhou's signature dish: a clear, aromatic beef broth with hand-pulled noodles, slices of daikon, cilantro, and a slick of fiery red chili oil on the side.
Wide flat hand-pulled noodles in a rich, milky lamb-and-mushroom broth with sweet potato vermicelli, tofu skin, and quail egg. Henan regional classic.
Northern-style boiled dumplings filled with seasoned ground lamb, scallion, and ginger. A Northwest China staple.
Pork, shrimp, and chive dumplings with a hint of ginger. A dim-sum favorite, available steamed or pan-fried.

pinyin: zhu rou bai cai jiao zi
intro: Classic boiled dumplings filled with ground pork and finely chopped napa cabbage. The everyday Northern Chinese jiaozi.
Northwest China style boiled lamb chunks served on the bone, eaten with the hands and dipped in salt and toasted cumin. Ningxia Hui specialty.
Beijing-style wok-fried lamb with thick-cut scallions in a savory brown sauce. Quick, smoky, and intensely savory.
Northwest Chinese style wok-fried lamb with toasted cumin seeds, dried chilies, and scallions. Fragrant, smoky, and addictive.

pinyin: bei jing tang cu li ji
intro: Crispy pork strips in a bright Beijing-style sweet and sour sauce. Milder and less fruity than the Cantonese version, with a sharper vinegar tang.

name_en: Guo Bao Rou (Crispy Sweet & Sour Pork)
intro: Dongbei (Northeast China) crispy twice-fried pork slices in a translucent sweet-sour glaze with ginger and garlic. Invented in Harbin in 1907.
Dongbei wok-fried eggplant, potato, and green pepper in a savory garlic sauce. A hearty vegetarian Northeast China classic.
Dongbei wide mung-bean noodles tossed with sesame sauce, shredded cucumber, carrot, and chili oil. A refreshing Northeast Chinese cold dish.
Soft silken tofu topped with sliced scallions, light soy sauce, and a drizzle of warm sesame oil. The Chinese proverb: 'one clear, one white, that's all you need.'
Smashed cucumber chunks with garlic, black vinegar, sesame oil, and chili oil. A refreshing Chinese cold dish from any province.
Crispy fried peanuts tossed with aged black vinegar, sliced scallions, cilantro, and dried chilies. A classic Shandong cold appetizer, often paired with beer.

name_en: Jing Jiang Rou Si (Beijing Shredded Pork)
intro: Shredded pork in a sweet bean sauce, served with scallion brushes and thin wheat pancakes for wrapping. Beijing's 'Peking duck' for the everyday table.

name_en: Yu Xiang Rou Si (Fish-Fragrant Shredded Pork)
intro: Sichuan shredded pork in a tangy, sweet-savory sauce with bamboo shoots, wood ear mushrooms, and carrots. 'Fish-fragrant' flavor — no fish, named for the seasoning used in traditional fish cookery.
Tender beef slices poached in a fiery Sichuan chili oil broth, layered over bean sprouts and crowned with chopped scallions. Sichuan classic.

name_en: Fuqi Feipian (Husband and Wife Beef Slices)
intro: Cold Sichuan appetizer of sliced beef offal in a chili-oil, Sichuan-peppercorn sauce with crushed peanuts and cilantro. Named for a husband-and-wife vendor pair in 1930s Chengdu.

name_en: Mao Xue Wang (Sichuan Blood Curd Hotpot)
intro: Chongqing-style fiery stew with duck blood curd, beef tripe, bean sprouts, and Sichuan peppercorns in chili oil. A Chongqing classic invented by dock workers in the 1920s.
Classic Sichuan peppery, vinegary thickened soup with shredded tofu, bamboo shoots, wood ear mushrooms, and a swirl of egg. A dim sum and banquet staple.

name_en: Yang Rou Pao Mo (Lamb Pita Bread Soup)
intro: Xi'an (Shaanxi) specialty: diners tear pita bread into pieces, then the kitchen soaks them in a rich lamb broth with glass noodles and tender lamb. Tang dynasty origins.
Cumin-spiced braised pork stuffed into a toasted crisp flatbread. Xi'an street food classic, dating to the Qin dynasty.
Extra-wide hand-pulled Shaanxi noodles in a spicy-sour chili oil sauce with soy, vinegar, and aromatics. Famous for the 58-stroke 'biang' character that's a Chinese tongue-twister.
Shanghainese steamed pork soup dumplings — eight pieces, each a delicate purse of dough holding a hot, savory pork jelly broth.
Shanghainese pan-fried pork buns with crispy sesame-seeded bottoms and a juicy pork filling. Six pieces, served with black vinegar.
Flaky pan-fried layered flatbread with sesame seeds and chopped scallion. Crispy outside, soft and chewy inside. The Chinese cousin of the croissant.

pinyin: bei fang shui jiao pin pan
intro: Mixed platter of pork-cabbage, lamb, and three-ingredient dumplings — a sampler to try multiple Northern Chinese dumpling styles in one order.
Henan street food: a flatbread split open and filled with a fried egg, scallions, cilantro, and chili sauce. Cheap, fast, and deeply satisfying.
Beijing glutinous rice rolls coated in soybean flour (the 'dust kicked up by the rolling donkey'), stuffed with sweet red bean paste. A traditional imperial-era snack.
Beijing imperial-style dessert: chilled yellow split pea pudding, smooth and lightly sweet, with a delicate floral fragrance. A favorite of Empress Dowager Cixi.
Beijing street snack: hawthorn fruits skewered and coated in glassy hard-crack sugar. Crack-shatter outside, sour-tart fruit inside.
Beijing traditional cooling drink: smoked plums, hawthorn, licorice root, sweet osmanthus, and rock sugar, served cold. Tart, sweet, and slightly smoky.
